parent.markdownDescription: Full id of a block to inherit from (`pack:name`). The parent definition is copied first, then this file's properties are applied on top. The parent is loaded first even if it is defined later in the pack.

caption.markdownDescription: Display name of the block (and its generated item). Default: generated from the id.
caption.description: Display name of the block (and its generated item). Default: generated from the id.

texture.markdownDescription:
Block texture name (name of the file in `textures/blocks/` with no path and extension included, just name)

Texture file must be a **png** image

Mutually exclusive with `texture-faces`.

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#texture)
texture.description:
Block texture name (name of the file in textures/blocks/ with no path and extension included, just name)

Texture file must be a png image

Mutually exclusive with texture-faces.

texture-faces.markdownDescription:
> **Important:** Can't be used if `texture` already specified

An array of 6 texture names for block sides.

Example:
```json
"texture-faces": [
    "grass_side",
    "grass_side",
    "dirt",
    "grass_top",
    "grass_side",
    "grass_side"
]
```

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#texture-faces)

model.markdownDescription:
Block model type from list:
- "block" - default block model
- "none" - invisible block (air)
- "X" - grass model (two crossed sprites)
- "aabb" - model based on block hitbox (complex hitbox will be combined into one). Examples: pipes, bulbs, panels.
- "custom" - used when specifying custom models via *model-name*

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#model)

model-name.markdownDescription:
In addition to built-in model types, you can use your own, loaded from file.

The property specifies the model name without `entry_point:models/` nor extension.

> **Warning:** Textures (materials) used in the model must be in the `blocks` atlas and specified in the *atlas-texture* format:
`blocks:texture_name`

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#model-name)

model-primitives.markdownDescription:
> **Warning:** The `model-primitives` property is deprecated. Use the [VCM format](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/vcm.md) for a textual description of the model's primitives.

Block model may be created with following properties:

```js
"model": "custom",
"model-primitives": {
    "aabbs": [
	    // list of AABB primitives
    ],
    // ... other primitives
}
```

**AABB** primitive is an array of values:
```
[x, y, z, width, height, depth, texture names for all 6 sides]
```

**tetragon** primitive (more like parallelogram) an array of three vectors, describing primitive position, X vector \* width, Y vector \* height.

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-models.md#block-models-deprecated)

culling.markdownDescription:
Face culling mode:
- **default** - normal face culling
- **optional** - face culling among blocks of the same rendering group can be disabled via the `graphics.dense-render` setting.
- **disabled** - face culling among blocks of the same rendering group disabled.

In `optional` mode, disabling `graphics.dense-render` will use the `*_opaque` texture variant (if available).

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#culling)

translucent.markdownDescription:
Enables translucency support in block textures (examples: water, ice).
Should only be used when needed, as it impacts performance.
Not required for full transparency (grass, flowers).

Default: `false`.

solid.markdownDescription:
Explicitly specifies that the block is solid - completely overlapping the blocks behind it.
Used by blocks with the `custom` model type, which must support culling of invisible geometry, as with the `block` type. If `false` specified then ignored.

Default: `false`.

rotation.markdownDescription:
Rotation profile (set of available block rotations and behaviour of placing block rotation) from list:

- "none" - no rotation available (default profile)
- "pipe" - wood logs, pipes, pillars
- "pane" - panels, doors, signs
- "stairs" - "pane" + flipped variants
- "ladder" - like a "pipe", but on horizontal surfaces it is installed like "pane"

particles.markdownDescription:
Particles are specified as a JSON object. Property names can be found [in the particles section](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/particles.md).

When camera is near to the block, the engine will create an emitter that will run
until the block is destroyed or the camera moves away a certain distance.

variants.markdownDescription: Variants 1..N (variant 0 is the block's root definition). Each variant starts as a copy of the root and may override `model`, `model-name`, `texture`, `texture-faces`, `model-primitives`, `culling` and `draw-group`. Up to 15 entries (16 variants in total).

state-based.markdownDescription:
Some properties can vary dynamically, depending on the variant number stored in the user bits of the block.

Variability parameters are specified in the `state-based` block:

```json
{
    ...
    "state-based": {
        "offset": 0,
        "bits": 4,
        "variants": [
            {...},
            ...
        ]
    }
}
```

- `offset` specifies the bit offset from which the variant index starts. (Default is 0)
- `bits` specifies the number of bits encoding the variant index. (Default is 4).
Currently, the maximum number of variants is 16, so specifying more than 4 bits does not make practical sense.

Properties available for variance:
- model
- model-name
- texture
- texture-faces
- model-primitives (deprecated)

Variants are managed via `block.set_variant(x, y, z, index)`.

### Custom model variants (geometry switching)

You can use different custom models for different variants. Provide a separate `model-name` for each variant that needs different geometry. The renderer caches geometry per (block id, variant).

The base model (specified in root) becomes variant 0. The variants array maps to indices 1+.

Example (default + two custom variants):
```json
{
    "model": "custom",
    "model-name": "stairs_middle",
    "state-based": {
        "bits": 4,
        "variants": [
            { "model": "custom", "model-name": "stairs_left" },
            { "model": "custom", "model-name": "stairs_right" }
        ]
    }
}
```

In this example:
- Variant 0 = `stairs_middle` (from root)
- Variant 1 = `stairs_left` (from variants[0])
- Variant 2 = `stairs_right` (from variants[1])

_Not available in `block.properties` (removed by `res/scripts/post_content.lua`)._

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#variants)

An array of 3 integers - R, G, B of light in range \[0, 15\]

hitbox.markdownDescription:
An array of 6 numbers describing an offset and size of a block hitbox.

The numbers are specified in the range [0.0, 1.0] - i.e. within the block (in the case of an extended block, the hitbox can be larger than one, but must not go beyond the "size" property).

Array *\[0.25, 0.0, 0.5,  0.75, 0.4, 0.3\]* describes hitbox width:
- offset 0.25m west
- offset 0.0m up
- offset 0.5m south
- 0.75m width (from west to east)
- 0.4m height
- 0.3m length (from north to south)

For composite hitboxes, the *hitboxes* property is used - an array of hitboxes, for example:

```json
"hitboxes": [
  [0, 0, 0, 1, 0.625, 1],
  [0, 0.6875, 0, 1, 0.3125, 1]
]
```

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#hitbox)

fields.markdownDescription:
Block fields allow you to write more data unique to a specified voxel than the user bits allow.

Block fields are declared in the following format:

```json
"fields": {
    "name": {"type": "data_type"},
    "array_name": {"type": "data_type", "length": "array_length"}
}
```

In addition to `type` and `length`, the `convert-strategy` parameter determines the value conversion strategy when narrowing the data type.

The parameter takes one of two values:
- `reset` - a value that does not exist in the new range will be reset to 0
- `clamp` - the value will be reduced to the closest one in the new range

Example: the number 231 when changing the field type from int16 to int8:
- in `reset` mode will turn into 0
- in `clamp` mode will turn into 127

Available data types:

| Type    | Size      | Description            |
| ------- | --------- | ---------------------- |
| int8    | 1 byte    | signed integer 8 bits  |
| int16   | 2 bytes   | signed integer 16 bits |
| int32   | 4 bytes   | signed integer 32 bits |
| int64   | 8 bytes   | integer signed 64 bits |
| float32 | 4 bytes   | floating-point 32 bits |
| float64 | 8 bytes   | floating-point 64 bits |
| char    | 1 byte    | character              |

- Currently, the total sum of the field sizes cannot exceed 240 bytes.
- A field without an array length specification is equivalent to an array of 1 element.
- A character array can be used to store UTF-8 strings.

Field names must not start with `.`; the total size of all fields must not exceed 240 bytes.

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#block-fields)

- reset - a value that does not exist in the new range will be reset to 0
- clamp - the value will be reduced to the closest one in the new range

Example: the number 231 when changing the field type from int16 to int8:
- in reset mode will turn into 0
- in clamp mode will turn into 127

Available data types:

| Type    | Size      | Description            |
| ------- | --------- | ---------------------- |
| int8    | 1 byte    | signed integer 8 bits  |
| int16   | 2 bytes   | signed integer 16 bits |
| int32   | 4 bytes   | signed integer 32 bits |
| int64   | 8 bytes   | integer signed 64 bits |
| float32 | 4 bytes   | floating-point 32 bits |
| float64 | 8 bytes   | floating-point 64 bits |
| char    | 1 byte    | character              |

- Currently, the total sum of the field sizes cannot exceed 240 bytes.
- A field without an array length specification is equivalent to an array of 1 element.
- A character array can be used to store UTF-8 strings.

Field names must not start with .; the total size of all fields must not exceed 240 bytes.

tags.markdownDescription:
Tags allow you to designate general properties of blocks. Names should be formatted as `prefix:tag_name`.
The prefix is optional, but helps avoid unwanted logical collisions. Example:

```json
{
    "tags": [
        "core:ore",
        "base_survival:food",
    ]
}
```

Block tags can also be added from other packs using the `your_pack:tags.toml` file. Example:

```toml
"prefix:tag_name" = [
    "random_pack:some_block",
    "another_pack:item",
]
"other_prefix:other_tag_name" = [
    # ...
]
```

_Not available in `block.properties` (removed by `res/scripts/post_content.lua`)._

base:loot.markdownDescription:
A list of tables with properties:

```json
{
    "item": "pack:item",
    "min": 1,
    "max": 3,
    "chance": 0.5
}
```

- `count` defaults to 1. It does not need to be specified if `min` and `max` are provided.
- `min`, `max` - the minimum and maximum quantity of the item.
- `chance` - the probability of the item dropping. Defaults to 1.0.

It should be noted that the `item` refers specifically to the item. That is, to specify the item of a block, you need to add `.item` after the block name. 
Example: `base:dirt.item`.

To generate loot, the function `block_loot(block_id: int)` in the `base:util` module should be used.

User property of the `base` pack.

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#loot---baseloot)

hitbox.markdownDescription:
An array of 6 numbers describing an offset and size of a block hitbox.

The numbers are specified in the range [0.0, 1.0] - i.e. within the block (in the case of an extended block, the hitbox can be larger than one, but must not go beyond the "size" property).

Array *\[0.25, 0.0, 0.5,  0.75, 0.4, 0.3\]* describes hitbox width:
- offset 0.25m west
- offset 0.0m up
- offset 0.5m south
- 0.75m width (from west to east)
- 0.4m height
- 0.3m length (from north to south)

For composite hitboxes, the *hitboxes* property is used - an array of hitboxes, for example:

```json
"hitboxes": [
  [0, 0, 0, 1, 0.625, 1],
  [0, 0.6875, 0, 1, 0.3125, 1]
]
```

Default: `[0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1]`.

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#hitbox)

textureFaces.markdownDescription:
> **Important:** Can't be used if `texture` already specified

An array of 6 texture names for block sides.

Example:
```json
"texture-faces": [
    "grass_side",
    "grass_side",
    "dirt",
    "grass_top",
    "grass_side",
    "grass_side"
]
```

Face order: `-x` (west), `+x` (east), `-y` (bottom), `+y` (top), `-z` (north), `+z` (south).

[Documentation](https://github.com/MihailRis/VoxelCore/blob/main/doc/en/block-properties.md#texture-faces)

Block model may be created with following properties:

```js
"model": "custom",
"model-primitives": {
    "aabbs": [
	    // list of AABB primitives
    ],
    // ... other primitives
}
```

**AABB** primitive is an array of values:
```
[x, y, z, width, height, depth, texture names for all 6 sides]
```

**tetragon** primitive (more like parallelogram) an array of three vectors, describing primitive position, X vector \* width, Y vector \* height.

- **default** - normal face culling
- **optional** - face culling among blocks of the same rendering group can be disabled via the `graphics.dense-render` setting.

In `optional` mode, disabling `graphics.dense-render` will use the `*_opaque` texture variant (if available).
